issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String, but the solution introduces a separate LectureName class and uses a field of type LectureName for lectureName. This is a structural type mismatch that changes the expected attribute type and introduces an extra class not present in the specification or template, potentially confusing students about whether lectureName should be a String or a LectureName object.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the types across all artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a String for lectureName (matching the UML and problem text) or update the problem statement and template to document and require a LectureName class and use it consistently in attributes, constructor parameters and accessors.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a constructor that initializes every attribute in the order shown in the UML (lectureName as a String followed by integers). The solution's constructor takes a LectureName object as the first parameter instead of a String, causing a constructor-signature mismatch with the specification and the expected order/types.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution constructor signature match the specification: accept a String lectureName followed by the integer attributes in the specified order. Alternatively, update the problem text/UML to specify LectureName as the constructor parameter type and ensure template and tests reflect that change.

issues.description: The solution declares getLectureName() with a return type of String but the backing field is of type LectureName; the getter and setter signatures in the solution also accept/return String while assigning/returning a LectureName instance. This causes an internal type/signature mismatch in the solution and contradicts the problem expectation (String), resulting in compile errors and confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the solution so getter/setter signatures and implementations match the actual lectureName field type. Either change the field to String and keep getLectureName()/setLectureName(String) as declared, or change the getter/setter signatures to use LectureName consistently (and update the problem/template to document this type if chosen). Ensure no mismatch remains between field type and method signatures.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect the lectureName attribute to be a String (lectureName: String), but the solution introduces a separate LectureName class and uses LectureName as the field type. This represents the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) with a different identifier/type across artifacts and may confuse students: they expect a simple String attribute but the solution models it as a LectureName object. The mismatch increases extraneous cognitive load because students must reconcile an unexpected custom type rather than following the straightforward String-based attribute described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent representation for the lecture name across artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field (matching the problem statement and template), or update the problem statement and template to explicitly introduce and use the LectureName class (and adjust getter/setter signatures accordingly). Prefer keeping lectureName as a String for minimal cognitive overhead unless the custom LectureName type is pedagogically justified.
